title: Eagles will not be punished for how team handled Jalen Hurts' blood clots situation, NFLPA responds - CBS Sports
description: The NFL concluded the process to clear Hurts for Week 5 in London was handled appropriately
body:
The NFL concluded the process to clear Hurts for Week 5 in London was handled appropriately
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Oct 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:46 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Philadelphia Eagles will not face any punishment from the NFL regarding how they handled Jalen Hurts' medical situation, according to The Athletic. On Monday, the team announced that Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season after blood clots were discovered in his lungs. The league has reportedly concluded that the process that led to Hurts being cleared to play in Week 5 vs. the Jacksonville Jaguars in London with a superficial blood clot "was handled appropriately." The league will not levy any punishment on the franchise for how it handled its medical process, or for Hurts not being given an injury designation ahead of the game. On Tuesday, the NFL released a statement providing more information on what it knew regarding Hurts' situation and the medical professionals treating him. The league says it was in contact with the Eagles during the tests, going back to the first one in London. The league also clarified what it called "misinformation" regarding reports that Hurts did not sleep for 36 hours ahead of their international game.Here is the full statement from the league:"The league had been in contact throughout the process with the Eagles medical personnel, and the Cleveland Clinic in London where the tests were conducted. The league's Chief Medical Officer Dr. Allen Sills arranges for medical resources with leading providers in every international market with approval from the NFL Players Association. Medical care for players is provided by club medical staff in coordination with independent doctors. There was also misinformation regarding Jalen not sleeping for 36 hours before the game. That was not true and no one told him not to sleep because of his situation. The club told all players, coaches and personnel to try to stay awake as long as they could on Saturday as the team was returning back home after the game in London. The team did not have a bye week and like other NFL teams that travel to London and back, they were trying maintain as much of a normal routine as possible."The NFL Player's Association (NFLPA), released a statement on Tuesday night responding to reports that the NFL will not punish the Eagles for the handling of the situation. They claim the league informed the union that they didn't plan to look further into the management and treatment of Hurts' health. The NFPA is asking the league to launch a full investigation.Here is the full NFLPA statement:
"The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts. In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward."On Thursday of last week, the Eagles issued a statement saying that a superficial blood clot in Hurts' calf experienced movement, leading the team to rule him out for their Week 6 matchup against the Carolina Panthers. The Eagles also revealed that the NFL was made aware of the situation last week. It was the first of several confusing developments that led to more questions than answers.Just days after Hurts' blood clot diagnosis became public, it was reported that the team did not plan to place him on injured reserve. Hours later, Hurts was being placed on injured reserve. Then came the bombshell on Monday, when a follow-up scan revealed Hurts' superficial vein thrombosis had developed into deep vein thrombosis, including "bilateral pulmonary emboli," meaning blood clots were now in both of Hurts' lungs.It's not exactly clear why Hurts was allowed to play a football game and take a long international flight with a superficial blood clot, or whether the Eagles' decisions made his situation more serious. But the NFL has concluded that the team took the appropriate steps in handling the issue. Jonathan Jones offered additional reporting to help clear up some misconceptions about this wild story.Was Hurts forced to stay awake in London?There was a report that Hurts was told by doctors not to sleep as a precaution due to his blood clot, so he didn't sleep for 36 hours before playing against the Jaguars. The NFL specifically targeted this rumor in their statement, making it clear that the team was encouraged to stay up late to remain on Eastern time.
Hurts was not told to stay awake because of his medical condition. He returned to the team hotel around 2:45 a.m. local time on Sunday and slept until around 10 a.m. Hurts also took a nap at the stadium before kickoff. Tom Pelissero eventually walked back this reporting, saying Hurts' agent clarified that while the quarterback was up until early Sunday morning being evaluated at a hospital, he was able to sleep before the game. Blood clot timelineSaturday, Oct. 10: Superficial blood clot discovered in Hurts' calf during a visit to the Cleveland Clinic in London following a team walk-through. 
Wednesday, Oct. 14: Follow-up appointment in Philly reveals superficial blood clot had moved, causing Eagles to shut down Hurts indefinitely. He undergoes further testing. Monday, Oct. 19: Eagles and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, issue a joint statement laying out the updated diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis. Here's the full statement:"Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition."Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. "blood thinners"). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football."Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects."

title: Michigan starting QB Tommy Carr vs. Indiana: What's next for Bryce Underwood? - CBS Sports
description: Carr's rise from freshman backup to Michigan starter signals a new direction for the offense and raises questions
body:
Carr's rise from freshman backup to Michigan starter signals a new direction for the offense and raises questions about Underwood's future in Ann Arbor
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:09 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Michigan Wolverines are expected to start freshman Tommy Carr on Saturday against No. 6 Indiana after he led a comeback win over Penn State last Saturday following the benching of former top recruit Bryce Underwood, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.Carr had a modest game passing the ball, completing 5 of 7 passes for 47 yards, but the Michigan offense operated much better with Carr under center, and he aided the rushing attack with four carries for 36 yards and the game-sealing touchdown. That performance was enough to convince Kyle Whittingham that it was time to make an official quarterback change in Ann Arbor, as Underwood will slide into the backup role for now.The grandson of legendary Michigan coach Lloyd Carr and the brother of Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr, Tommy Carr was a four-star recruit in the 2026 class out of Saline, Michigan, and opted to sign with the Wolverines, understanding he might not get the starting job until his junior year. However, with Underwood struggling, his opportunity comes much sooner than anyone -- including him -- was expecting, and now he'll live out his dream as the Michigan starter.
        
            
                Tom Fornelli's College Football Power Ratings: Ohio State falls from No. 1 amid Julian Sayin injury
                
                    Tom Fornelli                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Carr will be thrown into the fire against an Indiana team that will be looking to make a statement after letting their last game against Ohio State slip away. While the Hoosiers haven't been as dominant overall as their national title-winning squad from a year ago, the defense remains one of the best in the country, and the freshman will have his hands full. 
Why Michigan is making the change nowWhile Indiana isn't an ideal team for a freshman to make their first start against, making the change ahead of this game suggests it could be a permanent move.The move to Carr illustrates that Michigan recognized the struggles with Underwood as the starter were untenable. Michigan is 105th in the nation in scoring offense at 22.7 points per game, but even more than that, potential scoring drives have been negated by turnovers. With a defense that is good enough to compete in the Big Ten, the Wolverines cannot afford not to take care of the ball. Underwood completed just 58.1% of his passes for 924 yards, five touchdowns and six interceptions in his six starts. If you exclude the UTEP game, in which he completed 76% of his passes for 223 yards and two touchdowns, his completion percentage drops to 53.5%. 
From a financial perspective, benching Underwood is a stunner, but Whittingham has been hinting at a possible quarterback change since the opener, when Michigan barely escaped in a controversial fashion against Western Michigan on a last-second Hail Mary. It has been clear all season that Whittingham hasn't been thrilled with the offensive operation with Underwood under center, and despite his tremendous physical gifts, the Wolverines' offense has been both inconsistent and lacking explosive plays. It's one thing to struggle with accuracy if there are also big plays being produced, but Michigan is 119th in the nation in pass plays of 20 yards with just 13 this season. With Carr, Whittingham seems to be hoping to get a more consistent operation that can lean on the running game and keep things on track by being more accurate in the passing game. The message to the young quarterback will undoubtedly be that his job isn't to carry the Wolverines offense, but to simply help it be the best and most efficient version it can be. 
What's next for Bryce Underwood?The (quite literally) million-dollar question in this whole saga is what comes next for the former five-star recruit. Underwood was supposed to be the best quarterback Michigan's had in more than a decade, but instead he's become the face of disappointment in the NIL era. Michigan invested a ton of money to get Bryce Underwood to flip his commitment from LSU to stay at home and join the Wolverines, but after failing to show any real positive development over a season and a half as the starter, the Wolverines are moving on for now. It'll be fascinating to see what Underwood's value ends up being in the transfer portal -- assuming he does as expected and seeks a new opportunity this offseason. Plenty of coaches will still look at his physical skill set and believe they can do what Michigan failed to do under both Whittingham and Sherrone Moore, but his struggles may also preclude him from being considered by the truly elite programs. 
Plenty of top programs like Miami, Oregon, Indiana, Georgia, Texas, LSU and others figure to be in the market for a portal quarterback. But would any of those teams risk the downside of what we've seen to be Underwood's floor for the potential still in his physical abilities? Or, would he be better served trying to find a program with a proven track record of developing quarterbacks that might be more willing to roll the dice on the former five-star? Underwood could look at what's happening at Houston, where Connor Weigman has revived his career after struggling at Texas A&M to get the Cougars into the top 25 and the Big 12 title race. That kind of program might be the best fit for Underwood, who seems to need a serious time investment (not financial) from a program and coaching staff to drill into what he does best and how he can be successful.

title: Grading LeBron James' 76ers debut as Philly spoils Knicks' title celebration - CBS Sports
description: James stuffed the stat sheet with his usual all-around excellence in a 76ers win on opening night
body:
James stuffed the stat sheet with his usual all-around excellence in a 76ers win on opening night
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The biggest story of the offseason is now a regular-season reality. The new NBA campaign tipped off on Tuesday, and with it we got our first glimpse of LeBron James in a 76ers uniform. It went about as well as James and his new team could have possibly hoped in their inaugural outing together. The Sixers beat the Knicks 106-100, spoiling ring and banner night for the defending champions in Madison Square Garden. In 34 minutes, James supplied his usual all-around excellence by stuffing the stat sheet: 14 points, nine rebounds, seven assists and just one turnover. Here are our grades for James from his first game with Philly.Overall impact: AJames recently said the luxury of his game is that he can "literally do everything." He's not lying. James doesn't need to be the primary scorer to influence the proceedings and help his team win. That was true against the Knicks. He got off to a slow scoring start before finishing with 14 points on 5 for 13 shooting. He missed all three of his 3-point attempts. That's not great efficiency. It didn't matter. 
In 34 minutes, James had nine rebounds, seven assists and helped the Sixers' defense make life difficult on the Knicks, who shot just 37% from the floor and 33% from 3-point range. If those are the kinds of numbers and effort they can expect from the 41-year-old James going forward, Philly will happily take it.
Pregame pomp: ASelling James as a Sixer isn't a very heavy lift. You've got a franchise that hasn't been out of the second round in 25 years, and then the greatest player of all time comes along to save the day. The narrative writes itself. So do the hype videos. Put James in a sweatshirt with "Phila" across the front, have him do a little voice-over about being excited to play for something that's about more than just him, do some tracking shots of the city and the fans, and add a "throw the ball up" tagline. Boom. As they say in Hollywood, that's lunch. 
Slam Magazine also did a classic cover shoot with James. Full marks for going with "allow me to reintroduce myself," a line from Jay-Z's "Public Service Announcement," a track from "The Black Album," which was released in 2003, the same year James was drafted. 
The marketing machine has been in overdrive and won't be slowing down anytime soon. Cleared for takeoff: AEarlier on Tuesday, NBA commissioner Adam Silver was asked about the much-discussed matter of James flying in a helicopter provided by Fanatics as part of his endorsement deal with the company. Michael Rubin, a former Sixers minority owner and the CEO and founder of Fanatics, added some fuel to that particular conspiracy fire. And Pablo Torre, who won a Pulitzer for his reporting on the Clippers cap circumvention scandal, is looking into the matter. But to hear the commissioner tell it, he sees nothing untoward about the arrangement.
"In the case of LeBron and that helicopter, he has a deal with Fanatics. It's perfectly appropriate if part of his deal is they're gonna supply a helicopter to him," Silver said. "I mean, as long as it's just a deal between the Fanatics and LeBron and no team is involved, there's no rules issue there whatsoever." That has to come as a relief to James, whose commute from New York to Philly would get a lot more hectic if he had to travel up and down the New Jersey Turnpike. Gameday fit: BNot exactly his most memorable outfit. Nothing flashy here, just all business with a dark, double-breasted suit, a crisp white shirt and no tie to go with sunglasses and a bag. Vintage from head to toe.
24th season introduction: CThis one is complicated. James plays for the Sixers. He was introduced for the first game of his record-extending 24th NBA season in New York. That will automatically earn you some boos from the local fans, and rightly so. But James has often talked about how much he loves playing at Madison Square Garden, and there was quite a bit of chatter this offseason about how he dreamed of one day becoming a Knick. All of which led to a bit of a mixed reaction from the crowd when the PA announcer called his name as the fifth starter for Philly. Knicks fans can be forgiven for being uncertain about how to act on this one (though they stepped up their game later with a new chant).
Handshake with Joel Embiid: A+It's the first game and Embiid has already roped him into doing D-Generation X cosplay. No notes.
First Sixers chalk toss: AClassic.
First assist: BWhen asked during the preseason how he anticipated utilizing LeBron, head coach Nick Nurse pointed to James's playmaking and said he'd help initiate the offense. Makes sense. James is one of the best passers of all-time.
For his first assist in a Sixers jersey, James saw Jaylen Brown in the paint, found the right angle as he so often does, and made a quick entry pass for an easy bucket. Much like LeBron's gameday fit, it wasn't exactly flashy, but it worked.
First field goal: CAmong other things, James is the all-time leader in points and field goals made. This basket will…add to those numbers. Picking on Landry Shamet in the post probably isn't something that will make his career highlight reel, but James had to get his first basket somehow. 
First dunk: B-The business end of an alley oop off a pass from Brown. This is sort of graded on the LeBron curve. He's one of the most explosive dunkers ever, but he's also going to be 42 in December. As far as his all-time dunks go, this won't be that memorable, but it's still impressive how athletic the man remains. 
Running the break: AJames has been one of the best players in the open floor for nearly a quarter century. It's a sight to behold. Last season, he finished second in the NBA in total fastbreak points -- behind only new teammate Tyrese Maxey. In the third quarter, Maxey found him on a hit ahead and James did what he does best: accelerating toward the basket and finishing in transition at full speed. Josh Hart briefly made a half-hearted attempt at stopping the ball before thinking better of it. Smart man.
Correcting misinformed Knicks fans: A+If you're gonna trash-talk (arguably) the greatest player of all time, at least get the guy's bio right. As for LeBron, the surest way to win over Philly's collective heart is to yell at an overbearing Knicks fan on national TV. 
Spoiling ring night at MSG: UnknownDo they even make letter grades that go that high?

title: With loss to 76ers, Knicks get early reminder of how hard repeating will be - CBS Sports
description: The 76ers spoiled the celebration and reminded the Knicks that it's time to turn the page
body:
The 76ers spoiled the celebration and reminded the Knicks that it's time to turn the page
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:07 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        NEW YORK -- For 29 teams, opening night represents a new beginning. For one, it's closer to a conclusion. A period, or in the case of the New York Knicks, an exclamation point, at the end of a championship season. It was October for the Philadelphia 76ers on Tuesday, but for everyone else at Madison Square Garden, it might as well have been June 13.Fans were given mini championship banners upon entering the arena, a fitting token as roughly 20,000 awed onlookers watched the Knicks raise their first properly-sized championship banner in more than 53 years. The celebratory haze of New York's last game on that court, the legendary 29-point Game 4 comeback that gave the Knicks a nearly insurmountable NBA Finals lead, still hung in the air of the world's most famous arena. Even the team played along with gauche golden jerseys, as if they felt the need to wear last year's trophy on their chests.Whatever magic the Knicks captured en route to that trophy seemingly expired on Tuesday as the 76ers so helpfully reminded them that this is, in fact, a new season. Final score: 76ers 106, Knicks 100. It won't be as simple to survive Karl-Anthony Towns' foul trouble now that Mitchell Robinson is wearing green and white as a member of the Celtics. The Knicks won't overcome seemingly every single fourth-quarter deficit as Jalen Brunson so forcefully ensured last spring. And of course, the field this time around is a good deal stronger than it was during New York's last title push.

        
            
                Grading LeBron James' 76ers debut: The King gets sterling marks as Philly spoils Knicks' title celebration
                
                    John Gonzalez                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
In that sense, Philadelphia represented a fitting opponent for opening night. The Knicks tore through last year's 76ers like wet tissue paper. These are not last year's 76ers. The presence of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown meaningfully changed the equation on Tuesday, and it easily could do so in April and May as well. Look around the Eastern Conference and you'll find similar talent practically everywhere -- teams just as eager to knock the Knicks off of this perch.Kawhi Leonard is back in Toronto. Giannis Antetokounmpo will attempt to revitalize the Heat. Famed Knicks-slayer Tyrese Haliburton will make his long-awaited return from a torn Achilles tendon on Wednesday for the Pacers, and Celtics star Jayson Tatum, now presumably back to full strength after returning from his own Achilles tear last season, would surely love to exorcise his own Madison Square Garden demons in a rematch of the 2024 series in which he was injured in the first place. There are new challengers everywhere, all aiming for a Knicks team that now knows none of them can be taken for granted if they hope to hold their crown. Their captain, at least, is embracing the competition.
"I think it's good for us to kind of get knocked down off the mountain, humble ourselves, put our egos in check and see what's going to happen," Jalen Brunson said after Tuesday night's loss. "I've told you guys since Day 1: whatever happens these first couple of weeks of the season, that's gonna show who we truly are."He's right about that last part, as the NBA conveniently loaded the beginning of New York's schedule with exactly these sorts of tests. The Knicks see the 76ers again in 10 days. They'll face all seven of the teams widely projected to join them in the top eight of the Eastern Conference standings (the 76ers, Celtics, Pacers, Heat, Raptors, Pistons and Cavaliers) by Nov. 27, and will play those teams in 12 of their first 19 games. If these Knicks are up to the task, they'll prove it in the weeks to come.
        
            
                NBA 2026-27 season predictions: Expert picks for full standings and Finals
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Doing so will require far more disciplined play than they brought to opening night. Mike Brown said his team's transition defense was "not good," and that's an understatement by the standard this group set last spring. New York all but turned off the transition tap in the playoffs, allowing less than 10 fast-break points per game. By Brown's measure, the Sixers scored 19 in the second half. The Knicks shot just 17-of-29 in the restricted area, bleeding points on missed finishes at the basket. Towns' fouling came back to bite them in the second half when Andre Drummond, who miraculously posted a double-double in the first half alone, ran out of gas playing half of the game.
These are solvable problems. The Knicks were, obviously, great in transition in the playoffs, and Drummond was spectacular early in his Knicks debut before his minutes total ticked too high. It's easier to finish at the rim when you're making every 3 as the Knicks did in the playoffs. That wasn't sustainable, but there's a middle ground, and playing at a better, more intentional pace will help create cleaner looks at the basket. The Knicks, according to Brown, "looked like we were running in mud." From Game 4 of last year's Hawks series on, that wasn't a problem in the playoffs. It's easy to take that for granted on a single night out of 82, especially one earmarked for celebration.But the season they celebrated is over, and the 76ers gave the Knicks a harsh welcome into this new one. The "running in mud" version of the Knicks stands little chance in this Eastern Conference arms race. The championship bar is higher now, and the 2027 Knicks have a ways to go if they hope to clear it as easily as their 2026 counterparts did.

schema.headline: With loss to 76ers, Knicks get early reminder of how hard repeating will be - CBS Sports

title: If Barcelona and injuries can't stop PSG's pursuit of a UCL three-peat, can anyone? - CBS Sports
description: Even with Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia forced off, the back-to-back champions relied on suffocating
body:
Even with Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia forced off, the back-to-back champions relied on suffocating intensity and late goals to prove the gap to the rest of Europe remains wide
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:14 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The three-peat is on. Manchester City, Barcelona, injuries to key players: none of these can stop Paris Saint-Germain. Who or what else can?In the space of six days the back-to-back champions have produced passages on a par with anything that took them to glory in 2025 and 2026. Not complete performances, it should be said, but maybe that is what makes them so scary. They are a team that has so many different ways of winning. Once famed for their wastefulness, they spent half an hour at the Etihad last week showing they can make ball go goal from any angle at any moment.Tonight they took Barcelona's famed press and showed them what a throttling intensity really feels like. Eight times they recovered possession in the attacking third. Barca defenders aren't used to 75% pass completion around their own penalty area but any time the ball went to the full backs they were surrounded by blue shirts.PSG could bully-ball Barcelona, Lucas Hernandez rag dolling Anthony Gordon off a set piece and thundering a header in to put his side 2-1 up. One of the underrated qualities of this glamor outfit is the belligerence with which they hold their last line. When Fermin Lopez burst through it in the first half, Willian Pacho would not give up the chase. If he had to take a boot to the face to keep the ball out then so be it. Everywhere you looked PSG were chasing lost causes.
Don't let the scoreline trick you. What briefly looked like a your-ball, my-ball exhibition ascended into a brawl in a rooftop bar, a cocktail of muscularity and skill. The haymakers these two swung at each other left their mark. Dani Olmo lasted just 27 minutes for Barcelona, and by the hour, PSG had lost both Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. For the former it had the look of yet another hamstring injury but there will be serious concern about what appeared to be a knee injury for Kvaratskhelia after his clash with Xavi Espart.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            When we ask what might stop PSG joining the true greats of the continent with three straight European Cups, the obvious answer is that Kvaratskhelia's injury is as serious as it looks, that even with obsessive micromanagement of their minutes neither Nuno Mendes nor Dembele make it to the spring unscathed. On the evidence of tonight, it is not a given that that stops this team. Ferran Torres might not have scored but he did what Barcelona knew he can do at the highest of levels, get good shots in the box.Hernandez, a World Cup winner blighted by injuries, was perfectly suited to the muscularity required to defend Yamal. He did not get it perfect; no one can reasonably be expected to do so against the best forward in the world. However he held out for long enough that it took something quite remarkable to bring Barcelona level.
While this was a game won in the last 10 minutes, Vitinha volleying low past Joan Garcia before Fabian converted an Achraf Hakimi cross at the back post, PSG had made their point long before. They had kept on through the loss of those two star forwards. Barcelona had had their moments but the hosts had had the territory, the shots, the momentum. They had had nothing to prove and yet they did anyway. If the mentality of champions can shine through in what is fundamentally a low-stakes encounter for two teams who can cruise to the top eight should they feel it is necessary. PSG so often don't.As for their opponents, they could point to their own absences as having a telling impact. Raphinha was on the team sheet but the Raphinha seemed to still be dealing with the hamstring injury that he picked up over the international break. Rodri's heavy workload in that time also meant that he was rested, a decision Hansi Flick might have regretted in more pressurized circumstances. Breaking that PSG press requires the most adept of ball player at the base of midfield. If these two meet again the veteran midfielder could be the ace in the hole. Neutrals will hope they do. This was a better contest than required and came even as so many on both sides were off color. Not just Raphinha but Yamal too lacked punchiness. Vitinha was not quite himself either. And still PSG found a way to win. As if the rest of Europe needed any further warning, the supposed next best have just discovered how big the gap is to the champs.

title: NFL, Saints address plans for Paris game during Week 6 as protests escalate in France - CBS Sports
description: The league says its continuing with its original plans and monitoring the situation
body:
The league says its continuing with its original plans and monitoring the situation
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:26 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Protests escalated in France over the weekend over living costs and education, raising concerns over the NFL game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints scheduled to take place in Paris on Sunday. The unrest stems in part from citizens demanding better school conditions, teacher shortages and public services, but it has since grown as violent groups have rioted, clashed with police, and set fire to public buildings. At least 1,800 across the country, according to CBS News. Hundreds of thousands have taken to the streets across the nation to demand change from the government, as both protesters and law enforcement have turned to violent methods. Concern over player, personnel, and fan safety has become the main topic surrounding next week's international game, the first-ever regular-season matchup to take place in France.The league said they are increasing security for the game and said officials are collaborating with Parisian and national authorities overseas and the U.S. State Department, saying, "presence will be heightened."NFL Executive VP of club business, international and league events Peter O'Reilly provided a security update at the league's annual fall owners meeting. He said the league has had people in Paris for the last 10 days.
"There's nothing more important from our standpoint than the teams' security, the fans' security -- everybody involved with this game," O'Reilly said. "Obviously being very vigilant in everything we do, in all of our planning on an hour-by-hour basis, working closely with the two teams."He added, "We feel confident that we would not have any impact on the broader resources needed. That's always top of mind for us, and we feel confident that we wouldn't be depleting resources in a negative way around this game."O'Reilly said there was never a time when the league felt the game couldn't be played in Paris and that "all our plans for the Paris game are moving forward."
The league released a statement last week saying they still plan to conduct the game as scheduled on Oct. 25 and provided a similar update on Sunday after news of the social unrest spread."Preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France next Sunday," the NFL said. "We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We are also providing the two clubs with regular updates. There's been no disruption or impact at league sites."Saints executive Greg Bensel backed the league's statement and offered some insight into the league's safety precautions. 
"We concur with the NFL's statement and are planning to play the game. In addition to working closely with the NFL, we have also maintained daily security updates with our security partners in France," Bensel said. "Members of our football operations staff and internal security team have been on the ground in France for the past few days and there has been no disruption or impact at any of our team sites."Last week, the league's statement said, "We're excited for the first-ever regular season game in Paris, and preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France on October 25. As we do for every NFL game, including our international games, we work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We look forward to welcoming fans to Paris later this month."The game is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET, 2:30 p.m. local time. The league has changed games in the past due to various factors, including weather and field conditions, so it is not entirely out of the realm of possibility that the game could be moved. The Saints are considered the home team, so if they did move it, which they clearly do not plan to do right now, New Orleans would be the obvious new location.
While protests have taken over Paris, it's not the only place in France affected. Here's more from CBS News:"Authorities said masked groups on Saturday set fires and attacked public buildings, including city halls, in several cities."In Limoges, a city in central France, flames engulfed the 19th-century City Hall, causing its roof to collapse. Haute-Vienne prefect Maurice Barate told LCI television that the fire was deliberately set and nearly destroyed the building. The fire was under control Sunday.""Around Paris' Place de la République on Sunday morning, dislodged cobblestones, shattered storefronts and broken glass marked the aftermath of the events. Looting and damage were reported around the square and in some other tourist and shopping areas in the city center."Paris police said Sunday that 855 people were arrested in the French capital region alone. The Paris prosecutors' office said that 557 of them were kept in police custody."

title: Ohio State QB Julian Sayin out 'indefinitely' in blow to Buckeyes' CFP, national title hopes - CBS Sports

body:
OSU coach Ryan Day indicated the Buckeyes could be without their starting QB for the season

        Ohio State may be without star quarterback Julian Sayin for the remainder of the season in what could be a significant blow to its national championship hopes.Ohio State coach Ryan Day said Tuesday that Sayin would be out "indefinitely" and that may include the remainder of the season. No. 3 Ohio State will give both Luke Fahey and Tavien St. Clair first-team snaps this week during the bye week ahead of its next game against No. 16 USC on Oct. 31."Based on the nature of the injury we are putting together a plan for him not being available for the regular season and him also not being available for the postseason," Day said. "If he's not able to return this fall, we're putting together a plan for that, as well."
        
            
                2026 CFP bracket projection: How Julian Sayin's uncertain status could reshape Ohio State's playoff path
                
                    John Talty                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Sayin suffered an arm injury in the fourth quarter of the Buckeyes' 19-15 win over Indiana on Saturday. If Sayin is out for the remainder of the regular season, he would miss games against No. 16 USC, Oregon, Northwestern, Nebraska and Michigan. Before the injury, Sayin ranked third nationally in passing yards (2,007) and touchdowns (19). 
Impact on CFP seedingThe undefeated Buckeyes are in prime position to make the College Football Playoff – they are the No. 2 seed in CBS Sports' CFP bracket projections – but the selection committee will take into account the impact of no Sayin. Within the CFP protocol is the consideration of "the unavailability of key players and coaches that may have affected a team's performance during the season or likely will affect its postseason performance."If Ohio State's play suffers without Sayin, that can have an impact. If Sayin is indeed out for the season, that can have an impact. How long will Sayin' be out?If Sayin's progress improves and he is able to return this season – a seemingly unlikely proposition given Day's comments on Tuesday – Ohio State would likely get the benefit of the doubt if it lost a game that Fahey or St. Clair started against USC or Oregon. Conversely, that loss would take on even greater meaning if Fahey was expected to be the starter through the remainder of the season. 
Consider it this way: It would almost be as if the selection committee was evaluating different teams. There's the Ohio State with Sayin and the Ohio State without Sayin. If the latter looks noticeably worse than the former, it could have a significant impact. It is a situation that bears watching if Ohio State stays the course as a top playoff contender. If the Florida State playoff situation with Jordan Travis in 2023 has taught us anything, it is that a top team can be penalized if it is missing a key part of its offense. The undefeated Seminoles famously missed the four-team playoff in 2023 after Travis suffered a season-ending injury that the committee determined impacted FSU's outlook. If Ohio State doesn't look the same without Sayin, there is a precedent already for the Buckeyes to be penalized. There's a lot still to like about Ohio State, from Heisman Trophy frontrunner Jeremiah Smith to one of the nation's top defenses that is holding opponents to 13.4 points per game. But how the selection committee views Ohio State without Sayin is now the most interesting College Football Playoff subplot as the calendar turns to the back half of the season.

title: How FIU built a top-10 defense in 2026: Bounceback transfers, modular scheme - CBS Sports
description: Dewitt's top-10 scoring unit thrives on modular schemes and hometown transfers like sack leader Deejay Holmes to
body:
Dewitt's top-10 scoring unit thrives on modular schemes and hometown transfers like sack leader Deejay Holmes to fuel a defensive turnaround in South Florida
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:36 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        One of the best defenses in the Group of Six is a unit you don't hear much about nationally. Its coordinator, Jovan Dewitt, even calls them a "no-name, faceless defense." But the FIU Panthers have put together impressive performances this season while attempting to build on the momentum started in 2025. The individual stats aren't eye-popping, but as a collective, FIU is ninth nationally in scoring defense, 12th in passing yards allowed per game, and 24th in yards per game allowed. Their 3-3 start has seen every opponent except for Jacksonville State score 20 points or fewer. Now, as the faceless men look to the back half of their 2026 season, CBS Sports looks at how the unit was built and how it's powering FIU's success.Bounceback transfers and how they're built FIU has been a program of unrealized potential since Mario Cristobal was fired after one bad season in 2012. Cristobal went 7-6 with a conference title in 2010, then 8-5 in 2011, led by future pro receiver TY Hilton. Cristobal's journey led him to a national championship game appearance in South Florida -- but coaching the school a few miles away in Coral Gables. 
FIU backslid and languished between being below average and one of the worst teams in FBS. Butch Davis, a different Miami coaching legend, came to wrest the program out of freefall and did for two seasons before leaving in a blaze of glory in 2021, publicly blasting school administration on the way out. That made way for Mike Macintyre, who took over in 2022 right as the NIL era became supercharged and just a few years after the transfer portal's inception. His staff found an intriguing proposition for team building. Sure, perhaps they wouldn't be able to get a commitment from Deejay Holmes out of high school at powerhouse Pahokee High School. Holmes ended up signing with Ole Miss. But should he ever want to transfer home, they could be a landing spot. That's exactly what happened as Holmes found that Ole Miss wasn't the right place for him. He transferred back ahead of the 2026 season and has been FIU's anchor."Everyone at home can see me. They don't have to FaceTime me when I'm in Mississippi. You know, they can really see their baby boy now," Holmes said. 
It's a blueprint many G6 programs in metro areas use, and it's part of how they can survive in this roster-building environment. FIU has multiple players who fit that mold. Holmes and the defensive front power the position group and make it easier for the rest of the defense on the backend. "I would say I'm more comfortable in getting depth in my drops because I don't really have to worry about the quarterback escaping the pocket and running for like 15 yards, like how I was last year," linebacker Josiah Stewart said. "I don't mean that in no shade, I'm just more comfortable in my job." 
Holmes leads the team in sacks, and he says his mentality is shaped by the Chucky doll he's often seen carrying into the stadium on game days."Growing up, I just always remember like that doll was a killer. He had a passion for it, you know. I'm a killer on the field. That's how I feel. I really feel like it's my killer season," Holmes said.Modular defense in the portal era FIU went 7-5 and became bowl eligible for the sixth time in the program's 23rd season, and first under head coach Willie Simmons, who kept Dewitt from MacIntyre's staff when he took over. Dewitt says Simmons is a hands-off, CEO-style coach and gave him a simple message: Be simple, and make sure the base defense lives with four down linemen. 
Dewitt's had a winding journey. In 2019, while at Nebraska, he battled throat cancer, losing 100 pounds and confronting his own mortality more than any challenge an offense could pose. He still suffers from some neuropathy in his extremities, but otherwise he's healthy. Now he builds a defense built in what he calls a "modular fashion," understanding the challenges of being in the Group of Six.  "I think you have to really be smart or strategic in what you're trying to do and how you're trying to do it, because gone are the days where if you have a, like, we'll have players that we won't have next year for sure. Like, we have some really good players that will be gone in a year, so from that standpoint, I think you do have to be a little bit strategic in how you go about your process of teaching from the basic fundamentals all the way up to the, you know, the hardest red zone defense you want to think of," Dewitt said. You can take different chunks and pieces from different places and make them all fit. And so, what we try to do is we try to keep some congruencies throughout from the front end to the back end, so that we're not confusing people. And there's a bunch of the same principles all over the place. We can make something that looks really, really different to an offense, but for us it's the same concept. Look at it this way: if each position only had to learn three different techniques, you could run about 25 or 27 different calls."
On the backend, it's often a blend where one half of the secondary plays one type of coverage, and the other plays another. Gary Patterson is perhaps most famous for this style of coverage. Dewitt says his players are so in tune with the system they know what the call is before it comes in from the sideline. "We had a red zone period today, and I said, "What do you guys want? They're like, "Coach, you already know the call. I said, "You're right. Go ahead, run it."He's got heady players like Stewart and safety Shamir Sterlin, who are young but so adept at making sure everyone's in the right place that Dewitt says they rarely miss assignments. Stewart patterns his game off of Hall of Famer Luke Kuechly, not just on the field but off it as well. Kuechly is renowned for how he studies film and calls the offenses' plays out before they run it. Stewart tries to do the same. 
"Even today, I'm calling out like they're pistol, or FIB, and they run counter. I'm calling it out before it happens. I'm calling out draw, and all that extra stuff," Taylor said.Every moment of downtime can be spent watching film. Taylor says he multitasks between Call of Duty Warzone and College Football 27 sessions, although he doesn't love the new passing mechanics. Go balls were easier in last year's version. While Taylor is struggling with the concepts in a video game, in real life, it's what the Panthers are best at. Concepts being at the bedrock of the defense allow for them to adjust to surprises from offenses, versus rigid rules that are made to be broken. The offense has to improve for FIU to get where it wants to go, but the foundation the defense is building is a great start for the Panthers. 
"They're not worried about stats," Dewitt said. "They just want to win games. They just want to play well enough to win games. So they're not worried about what the stat sheet says or where we rank. And they're just not concerned with that. They just want to play. Did we play well enough? We have standards, not goals. Did we play well enough to win the game? If we did, whatever the outcome, we can live with it. If we didn't, then we have a problem."

title: LSU basketball roster tracker: Who's eligible to play for Will Wade in 2026-27 season? - CBS Sports
description: With the 2026-27 college basketball season now less than two weeks away, LSU coach Will Wade is still trying to finalize his roster. How
body:
With the 2026-27 college basketball season now less than two weeks away, LSU coach Will Wade is still trying to finalize his roster. However, Wade received more clarity on Tuesday on who will and won't be eligible. RJ Luis Jr., who was perhaps the most controversial player seeking a fifth year of eligibility, will not be eligible to play for the Tigers this season, sources told CBS Sports's Matt Norlander on Tuesday. As a result, LSU coach Will Wade has given up his months-long fight on Luis' behalf.While Luis won't be eligible for the season, two international players will be providing more clarity in Baton Rouge. Brice Dessert is expected to be eligible, while Saliou Niang — a former second-round pick in the 2025 NBA Draft — has already been cleared, Norlander reported.A 6-foot-8 wing, Niang is an explosive athlete who should be in line to start for the Tigers this season. Niang was named the Italian Lega A Most Improved Player in 2025 before declaring for the 2025 NBA Draft. However, he didn't sign an NBA contract, which gave him a path to become eligible.Niang and Dessert would join Michael Ružić, who was cleared to play ahead of LSU's first scrimmage of the season. The Tigers had 10 players listed on their roster for the first scrimmage earlier this month.

        
            
                RJ Luis ruled ineligible at LSU, but Saliou Niang and Brice Dessert will both be on Tigers' roster
                
                    Matt Norlander                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Last month, news broke that Márcio Santos — a player LSU recruited and hoped to get eligible for the upcoming college basketball season — had signed a two-year contract with Kosner Baskonia, a professional team based in Spain. Santos was part of LSU's intentional recruiting class that featured five players: Santos, Niang, Brice Dessert, Ružić (Joventut Badalona) and Gilad Levy, a 7-foot-3 center from Israel. Wade spoke to reporters for the first time this offseason last month and called his roster and how they're going about the process "unconventional.""What we're doing is unconventional," Wade said. "I understand that. But, 20 years ago, Airbnb was unconventional. Everybody stayed in a hotel. Fifteen years ago, you rode in a taxi everywhere. Now you take Uber. So, like, just because it's unconventional doesn't mean it's not going to work. Now, it may not work. If it doesn't work, write about what an idiot I am. I understand that. But just because it's unconventional, like I told our guys, we're going to be unconventional. We're going to be unapologetic about it. It is what it is. We're going to be unapologetic. This is who we are. This is what we're doing. This is the path that we charted. We're going to go down it."

        
            
                Will Wade explains LSU's 'unconventional' four-player roster: 'We're going to be unapologetic about it'
                
                    Cameron Salerno                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
So, who is eligible to play and who is still in eligibility limbo? Here is where every player on LSU's roster stands right now.Incoming transfers Skyy Clark (Transfer from UCLA)Current status: Eligible for nowClark is currently cleared to play by the California court. Clark, who previously played for Illinois, Louisville and UCLA, is coming off a season in which he averaged 11.5 points, 2.0 assists and 1.2 steals in 26 games. As a freshman at Illinois, Clark appeared in just 13 games and left the program midseason, citing personal and family reasons.Donovan Dent (Transfer from UCLA)Current status: Eligible for now*Dent was a preseason CBS Sports All-American after transferring to UCLA from New Mexico last season. Dent, who is one of the best pure point guards in the sport, initially retired after the conclusion of this past season from basketball but decided to pursue a fifth year of eligibility. If he's cleared, he would have a strong argument as LSU's best player.
Mouhamed Dioubate (Transfer from Kentucky)Current status: Cleared to playDioubate will be playing for his third SEC school this season after stops at Alabama and Kentucky. He transferred from Alabama to Kentucky last offseason and made 31 appearances (10 starts) for the Wildcats. Dioubate will likely be in the starting lineup on opening night.Divine Ugochukwu (Transfer from Michigan State)Current status: Cleared to playUgochukwu will be playing for his third school in three years, following stops at Miami and Michigan State. Last season, he started 12 games for the Spartans and averaged 5.1 points, 1.5 rebounds, and 1.5 assists.Abdi Bashir Jr.  (Transfer from Kansas State)Current status: Cleared to playBashir is one of the best 3-point shooters in college basketball. However, like most players in eligibility limbo on LSU's roster, it wasn't that simple. SEC commissioner Greg Sankey has been outspoken about Luis' case and filed an affidavit asking the court to uphold NCAA rules that prevent athletes from returning to the college level. The SEC also drafted new rules that prevent players, like Luis, who previously declared for the draft or signed a professional contract, from returning to college.

title: UFC 333: Movsar Evloev ready to fulfill destiny as champion after years of waiting - CBS Sports
description: After countless others jumped the line, Evloev finally has his shot to take the crown as best in the world
body:
After countless others jumped the line, Evloev finally has his shot to take the crown as best in the world
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:13 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Movsar Evloev believed he was destined to become UFC featherweight champion no matter how long it took. After years of patiently waiting for his opportunity, Evloev challenges Alexander Volkanovski on Saturday at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi. It's a fight that could cement Evloev's place among the division's elite while bringing an unceremonious end to one of its greatest careers. Volkanovski is a beloved, longtime champion enjoying a second reign in the twilight of his career. Evloev respects him immensely and takes no joy in accepting the role of kingslayer.Evloev's journey to the title took far too long, considering how dominant he's been. Twenty professional wins, half of which happened inside the Octagon, without a single defeat. His suffocating wrestling and soft-spoken personality make him hard to market, despite nearly 2 million Instagram followers and a fanbase that respects his talents. He's watched other fighters jump ahead of him in the title picture, including Diego Lopes, who got a second shot at Volkanovski shortly after decisively losing their first meeting.Evloev never fussed. If the UFC wanted more from him, then so be it. He wasn't concerned about how long it took or how many contenders he'd need to beat. Evloev knew the championship would eventually be his. Pay attention to how he talks about Saturday's fight. He clearly already considers the belt his.
"It'll feel like everything that came before was for a reason," Evloev told CBS Sports. "I'm not here just to be a UFC fighter. I know a lot of people who dream of signing with the UFC and don't think about the title. When I signed with the UFC, I already knew I needed to fight for the title, and I'd do anything to get there. I was patient. Now I'm here, and I'll fight for my title soon."Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC 333 for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!
Volkanovski has other plans. The two-time featherweight champion is aware that his best years are behind him. His body doesn't cooperate like it used to, particularly his chin, but he believes his skills and experience make him uniquely equipped to handle Evloev. The ailing king thinks he'll turn back time against his most deserving challenger.
"I truly believe that after this fight, people will say that this is the best version of Alex they've ever seen," Volkanovski told Megan Olivi. "I'm not saying that because I'm in my prime. I'm saying that because, stylistically, in the fight that I'll bring and he brings, I'll have that type of performance. People will say, 'Wow, I didn't expect that. Not at 38 years old.' I truly believe that." Evloev isn't convinced. In fact, he questions whether Volkanovski has been giving his own preparation the attention it deserves. The champion recently helped Mauricio Ruffy prepare for his fight against Arman Tsarukyan, splitting his time between his own career ambitions and his teammates."I hope when he talks like that, he believes it," Evloev said. "He was focused on Ruffy's camp. He'd do better to focus on his own fight. Of course, he's a great fighter. He's one of the best featherweights in history. That motivates me to prove to people I'm not fake. I'm not here [only] to fight. I'm here to win the belt and stay as long as we can."
Volkanovski is confident he can counter Evloev's wrestling after twice challenging Islam Makhachev for the lightweight title. Although he lost both of those fights, he gained valuable experience against one of MMA's most skilled grapplers. Volkanovski believes the two encounters sharpened his wrestling defense enough to keep Evloev from dictating where the fight takes place.On the feet, Volkanovski has the more sophisticated arsenal. He's a considerably more accomplished striker than Evloev, and the challenger isn't known for his knockout power. If Volkanovski can keep the fight standing, there's good reason to favor the champion.  Evloev disputes both assessments. He argues that his wrestling presents different problems than Makhachev's. And while he expects to take Volkanovski down repeatedly, he doesn't fear the champion's striking.
"My wrestling is different. My takedowns are different. I have good timing," Evloev said. "Even if I'm not able to hold him there to control him, I'm going to take him down as long as needed. For 25 minutes. It's not just wrestling. My striking is getting better, too. He's not so special that I'd avoid his striking and jump straight to wrestling."Evloev has spent plenty of time thinking about what comes after Saturday. First, tiramisu. It'll be how he celebrates winning the UFC championship and breaks a three-year abstinence from added sugars. More importantly, he wants to defend the title frequently and welcomes anyone willing to challenge him. He credits Volkanovski with being one of the few athletes who actually wanted to fight him, a quality he plans to inherit from his soon-to-be predecessor."After that, I want to beat everyone. I welcome everyone," he said. "I want to be a champion who stays busy. Of course, I respect him. He's the only champion who called my name. I only have respect for him." 
Evloev has a quiet confidence that sometimes gets lost behind his reserved demeanor. He's also funnier than people realize, something that's becoming increasingly apparent as his English improves. Take his reaction to Jean Silva demanding the next featherweight championship, for example. "I don't understand barking dogs. When dogs bark, you leave them alone," Evloev said with a smirk. "He's a great fighter, by the way. He's also welcome [to fight me] when I win the belt."Evloev was similarly unimpressed by Tommy McMillen, the outspoken featherweight prospect who recently criticized Evloev's fighting style as boring and petitioned to serve as the backup for Saturday's main event. McMillen has attracted considerable attention, but Evloev wasn't impressed by his recent performance against Marwan Rahiki.
"This guy, [Rahiki], almost beat him. I think he would've won if he didn't get tired in the third round..." Evloev said. "I'm here to test guys like him. I'm ready."First, beating Volkanovski is much harder. The champion has acknowledged that retirement is approaching. He's unwilling to continue fighting if he can no longer compete at the highest level, though he's convinced Saturday will demonstrate how much he has left. Volkanovski believes he can deliver a performance that makes people forget his age, at least for one night.Evloev has a different vision. He's waited too long for his opportunity to let sentiment interfere with his plans. Still, there's something bittersweet about potentially becoming champion at the expense of a fighter he admires, particularly if defeating Volkanovski convinces "The Great" to retire. 
Evloev doesn't like the thought of being responsible for that decision, but he agrees Volkanovski has nothing more to prove. Evloev would find some comfort in seeing Volkanovski enjoy the life he's built outside of the Octagon. Maybe even spend some time together without having to punch each other in the face. "I'd feel sad about that. I want to see more of his fights," Evloev said. "I think he's proved enough. It's better to enjoy the rest of his life, not just fighting. He's cooking well. He can do this. I wish that, after the fight, I could travel [to Australia] so we can cook together and eat good steak."

title: Knicks pause contract extension talks: Is Josh Hart's time in New York running out? - CBS Sports
description: Coming off a title, four Knicks players are eligible for contract extensions, including Karl-Anthony Towns and Jo
body:
Coming off a title, four Knicks players are eligible for contract extensions, including Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:21 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Perhaps only the New York Knicks could harsh the vibes of a championship run before even beginning their title defense season. Four notable members of the team, Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart, Miles McBride and Tyler Kolek, are eligible for contract extensions. While keeping the whole team together was always going to be a long shot, the Knicks announced earlier this month that they would be tabling all talks until later in the season, forcing all four players to open the season with uncertain financial futures.But what does this actually mean for the Knicks, who open their season Tuesday night against LeBron James and the 76ers at Madison Square Garden? Here are three quick takeaways on New York's sudden financial predicament.1. Knicks lose critical option on new Towns dealFor now, the question with Towns remains less about whether he'll get a new deal from the Knicks and more about what that new deal will mean for everyone else. Towns is irreplaceable. There is no other offensive center like him in basketball that has not already won an MVP or will inevitably win one in the near future. New York let its only other viable starting center option, Mitchell Robinson, leave in free agency, and as we've learned from deals involving players like Ivica Zubac and Walker Kessler, getting a high-end starter at center, even below the superstar level, costs draft capital the Knicks frankly do not have. They'll figure something out with Towns. It's just a matter of when and what.

        
            
                Knicks pause contract negotiations with Karl-Athony Towns, Josh Hart, others until 'later in the season'
                
                    Robby Kalland                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The Knicks have hoped to get Towns to take a substantial discount, as Jalen Brunson has. While he seems receptive to taking a deal below his $276 million max, the Knicks have seemingly not come close to an actual deal for him. While Friday's news doesn't necessarily preclude a below-market agreement down the line, it does deprive the Knicks of a critical bit of flexibility in how that deal is structured.Players with multiple years left on their contracts cannot extend during the season. Before the season, however, extensions are fair game. This matters for Towns because he has a $61.6 million player option for the 2027-28 season. If Towns and the Knicks had gotten a deal done before the season, they could have essentially used that option to front-load Towns' new contract and have his salary decline meaningfully from there. However, should he sign an extension during the season, he would have to decline that option, and his new contract would have to be more balanced. A player's salary cannot increase or decrease by more than 8% annually within a single contract. Major raises and dips must be part of a new contract or extension.
Why is this a potentially preferred contract structure? Because New York's financial cliff isn't coming in the 2027-28 season. It comes a year later in the 2028-29 campaign. That's when Brunson and OG Anunoby will start new deals thanks to their player options. Brunson has already taken a substantial discount once. Don't expect him to do it again. Anunoby is about as irreplaceable as non-All-Stars get. Using that option, the Knicks could have gotten the most expensive year of a new Towns deal out of the way and saved as much flexibility for what comes after as possible.This format isn't necessarily off the table. Towns could simply pick up his player option in the offseason and try extension talks again at that point. His value could also dip during the season, allowing the Knicks to re-sign him on more favorable terms. But it's always easier to get an extension done early when possible. The last thing the Knicks should want is their back-to-back title bid ruined by contractual sour grapes. In a perfect world, the Knicks would have preferred to have something done by now. This might not be their preferred structure, as a lower 2027-28 salary would make it easier to duck next year's second apron. But taking the option off the table, if only temporarily, costs the Knicks the flexibility they would probably have preferred.
2. It's time to start questioning Hart's future in New YorkWe should assume that Brunson's next deal will approach 35% of the cap. His discount won the Knicks a championship. Towns won't be quite that high, but it won't be far off either. Anunoby's player option for the 2028-29 season will pay him an estimated 26.2% of the cap, so a new deal probably starts in that range. Mikal Bridges is locked up at around 21% of the estimated cap at that point. Start doing the math. You're looking at around 110 to 115% of the cap for your top four players once everyone's deals are finalized. You should also assume that those deals are paying for fewer valuable years than their existing contracts do. Anunoby is going into his age-29 season. Brunson and Anunoby will play their age-30 seasons this year, and Towns his age-31 season. At best, you're paying for the back half of their prime. At worst, there will be real age- and injury-related decline. If the Knicks are going to continue competing for championships, they need to acknowledge that they probably need more than they currently have to do it (especially with Robinson already gone) and that they have less financial wiggle room to pursue possible upgrades.So where does that leave Hart, the fifth starter and the heartbeat of the team? A lot depends on what sort of extension he's willing to take. The Knicks have a bit more flexibility on this front than with Towns because he has a team option rather than a player option. The Knicks could use that option to leverage their way into more favorable terms.
Still, Hart is the oldest of the five Knicks starters. He'll turn 32 during the season. His game is probably the least likely to age well, given his inconsistent shooting and borderline reckless physicality he plays with. The old axiom is that it's better to move on from a player a year too early than a year too late. It's hard to imagine the Knicks moving Hart this season as they pursue back-to-back titles, but hesitance on a long-term extension afterward would be understandable.There isn't an in-house replacement ready. The Knicks under two different head coaches have resisted playing McBride with the starters because of how small his backcourt pairing with Brunson would be. Landry Shamet's shooting is nice in small doses and he's improved significantly as a defender, but similar problems exist there, and durability has been a concern for him. Perhaps the best possible developmental curve for promising second-round pick Mohamed Diawara could see him turn into a starter, and he's locked into a cheap, long-term deal, but he's a long way from adequately replacing Hart.Realistically, the Knicks would either have to stumble into a player we don't see coming or make a trade involving their precious remaining draft capital (at this point, their only tradable first-rounder is in 2033), ideally for someone on a rookie deal now. This front office has surprised plenty of times, but at this moment, Hart is still essential to New York's championship upside. The more costly Towns becomes, though, the more realistic breaking up this starting lineup becomes. You can't keep everyone in the apron era, especially if you want to maintain any level of depth.
3. Deuce McBride is the likeliest trade candidateMcBride will almost certainly be the cheapest of the three Knicks we've covered thus far on his next deal. He certainly is on his existing contract. The Knicks wisely extended McBride on very team-friendly terms right after trading Immanuel Quickley, knowing that he had a bigger role upcoming. If they extend McBride before Hart, that might be a tell that they're considering repeating that process with him stepping into a starting role afterward.
In reality, though, we have to assume that Hart will be a higher priority than McBride. In that case, McBride represents an expiring contract at New York's deepest position. The Knicks have Shamet, Jose Alvarado and Kolek as viable backcourt reserves. Meanwhile, they have little frontcourt depth behind Towns -- even with James Wiseman earning the final roster spot -- making McBride an obvious trade candidate to potentially fill that hole.

        It has been a difficult year at the running back position. Two of the teams on bye this week are part of the reason why. Omarion Hampton was supposed to be a top-12 running back but instead, he's found himself in a full-blown committee in one of the worst offenses in football. The Commanders don't have one running back on the roster averaging double-digit PPR Fantasy points. In other words, Fantasy managers won't miss them during their bye week. They will, of course, miss James Cook and Bhayshul Tuten, who are also on bye.The story of the week is the running backs we're getting back, though, to be fair, Jordan Mason will be more of a nuisance to Aaron Jones than a help to your Fantasy teams. The other two guys we are projecting to return, Josh Jacobs and Zach Charbonnet, are more exciting for the long term. Early in the week, I am ranking Jacobs and Charbonnet as high-end flexes and projecting them to get 10-12 touches in their debut. Though I am starting to wonder if that is too low for Jacobs.Jacobs will face the Lions in one of the highest projected scoring games of the week. Detroit has been an uneven run defense this year and an awful pass defense. James Cook and Chuba Hubbard had massive days against this defense, while the Cardinals and Jets running backs struggled. Travis Etienne was bad as a rusher but caught seven passes and scored 14 PPR Fantasy points. Because of the high total, I do think Jacobs could get into the end zone, which is why I rank him a handful of spots ahead of Charbonnet. More important for both backs is getting through the weekend healthy. For the rest of the season, I could see Jacobs as a high-end RB2 and Charbonnet as a top-24 back.QB | RB | WR| TENow let's get to the rest of the Week 7 RB preview:
